note: The review-and-choose board (task T50, session arena/dc72a69e-zone2). Every row is a proposal and nothing more: nothing here has been implemented. 'recommended' is this session's judgement, labelled as one, and is not a program fact. 'blockers' name the questions that must close first. 'relates_to' links each row back to the proposal on an inherited board it touches (SG- at pages/suggestions.html, P- at console/suggestions.html, DS- at marketing/improvements.html, R- at audit/suggestions.html), so this board adds rows without ever becoming a second copy of one. Cost and risk are coarse reviewer estimates in working time, also labelled as estimates.

state_values.proposed: On the board. No owner choice recorded.
state_values.blocked: Cannot be decided until the named question is answered.
state_values.chosen: Owner picked an option. Not yet built.
state_values.rejected: Owner declined. Kept on the board so it cannot be re-proposed.

decision_sheet.how_to_record: Open brief/data/decisions.json, set the row's 'choice' to the letter of the option you want, add a note, and set decided_by and decided_on. The next build re-renders the board with the choice shown on the row. Or tell the agent the IDs and it will record them in the same form.
decision_sheet.order: The rows are listed in the order that unblocks the most. DB-06 and DB-01 are prerequisites for almost everything else: one declares what the site is, the other removes the label that makes it read as generated from the pages T55 did not rebuild.

proposals.title: Stop describing the site as AI-powered on the operator and companion pages
proposals.what_changes: Remove 'AI-powered' and 'AI-powered Amazon affiliate' from the 14 pages that still print them: console/, research-hub/, summary.html, review-trace.html, affiliate-lab/, zone2/. The T55 rebuild already cleared every reader-facing page on 2026-11-16.
proposals.why: It is the brief's vocabulary surviving into the deliverable, and it is the strongest single signal that the copy was produced from a commission rather than from the work. Google's guidance names the risk it invites (BR-13); Amazon's content bar asks for robust original content (BR-08). No reader has ever chosen an affiliate site because it was AI-powered.

options.label: Remove from every public page; keep one note on the owner console
options.tradeoff: Reader-facing copy loses the claim entirely; the provenance is still recorded where only the owner looks.

options.label: Remove everywhere, including owner surfaces
options.tradeoff: Cleanest, but loses the record of how the pages were produced.

options.label: Keep, and add a sentence explaining what is and is not automated
options.tradeoff: Honest, but puts the word back in front of the reader, which is the problem.

proposals.effort: estimate: under an hour; a find-and-replace plus a read of each affected page
proposals.risk: estimate: none to compliance. A cosmetic risk that some pages read plainer.
proposals.sequence: 2 — the reader-facing half is already done by T55

proposals.title: Correct the overclaim wherever it survives, now that the landing page has been rebuilt
proposals.what_changes: T55 removed the 'Three listings identified' heading from index.html. What is left is DR-1's discipline applied to the owner-facing pages: no page anywhere may state the mapping as fact while F-03 is open.
proposals.why: The hero currently introduces the platform and then states its integrity policy; the reader is third. And the second heading asserts the one thing the project's own register declines to assert (FB-05).

options.label: Apply the rewrites as written
options.tradeoff: Faster; the copy is on the design-prompt page and can be checked against the spec rows.

options.label: Apply the correction only, leave the hero
options.tradeoff: Removes the overclaim, keeps the self-describing opening that reads as generated.

options.label: Commission new hero copy from the publication's own voice
options.tradeoff: Best fit with Counter Notes, but costs a writing pass.

proposals.effort: estimate: one to two hours including a re-read of every number in the replacement copy
proposals.risk: estimate: low. The rewrite introduces no new value that is not already published with a source.

proposals.title: Replace the abstract headings that survive on the operator surfaces
proposals.what_changes: T55 renamed the landing page's headings ('The short version', 'Start with the question, not the product'). The same treatment is still owed to the operator namespace, whose pages carry headings like 'Position at a glance' and 'What this platform is'.
proposals.why: A heading that names the artifact is a heading generated from a schema. A heading that names the buyer's question is a heading a person wrote (RV-11, DT-2).

options.label: Rewrite the four self-describing headings on the landing page
options.tradeoff: Small change, most of the effect.

options.label: Rewrite headings across the whole owner-facing namespace
options.tradeoff: Consistent, but touches 39 generated pages and their builder.

proposals.effort: estimate: under an hour for A; a day for B

proposals.title: Move the disclosure into the recommendation block instead of the page footer
proposals.what_changes: Every product recommendation renders inside a bordered block that carries the §5 sentence above the verdict, not in a strip at the top or a line at the bottom.
proposals.why: Both governing sources ask for proximity to the endorsement, not presence on the page: the Operating Agreement says 'clearly and prominently' (BR-05), and the FTC says the disclosure 'should be placed with the endorsement message itself' and is 'likely to be missed' at the end of a post (BR-17). The site currently satisfies the letter and misses the point.

options.label: Disclosure inside every recommendation block
options.tradeoff: Repeats the sentence on pages with several recommendations, which is what the FTC wants.

options.label: Disclosure at the top of the page and inside the first recommendation only
options.tradeoff: Less repetition; weaker on the second and later recommendations.

proposals.effort: estimate: half a day across the marketing templates
proposals.risk: estimate: low, and it reduces compliance risk rather than adding it

proposals.title: Make the blank cell a designed state rather than an absence
proposals.what_changes: An empty cell renders as an en-dash on a dotted rule, with a tooltip and a visible legend naming which rule or absence makes it empty. Three semantic states across the whole site: sourced (ink), blank (muted), conflict (amber, both values shown).
proposals.why: The site's discipline is its differentiator, and it currently renders as a gap. Google's own description of a good affiliate page is a page that adds value (BR-12); a blank with a stated reason is added value, a bare dash is not.

options.label: Full three-state treatment with a legend on every table
options.tradeoff: Best signal; a legend on every table costs a little vertical space.

options.label: Tooltip only, no visible legend
options.tradeoff: Tighter, but the reason is invisible on touch devices.

proposals.effort: estimate: a day across the table components

proposals.title: Declare one site, and demote the other thirteen to linked evidence
proposals.what_changes: Pick the reader-facing surface as the declared Site. Every other namespace stays published but becomes reachable only from it. Sixteen surfaces publish today — two more than before T55 and this namespace landed.
proposals.why: Google's people-first guidance names as a warning sign content 'spread across a large network of sites, so that individual pages or sites don't get as much attention or care' (BR-15). This repository publishes 14 surfaces (RV-16). Amazon's application asks for the Site list to be kept current and to name exact URLs (BR-10's page), and RR-11 on the readiness board is already a GAP for exactly this reason.

options.label: Counter Notes (marketing/) is the site; everything else is evidence behind it
options.tradeoff: Cleanest for an application, and the only surface already written for readers. Costs a navigation rebuild.

options.label: Keep the root dashboard as the site and fold the editorial into it
options.tradeoff: Preserves the work already done on the dashboard, but the dashboard is the surface that reads as generated.

options.label: Leave fourteen surfaces and declare the root URL only
options.tradeoff: No work, but the owner is submitting a site whose own architecture contradicts the content bar.

proposals.risk: estimate: medium — it is the largest change on this board, and it touches navigation that five namespaces depend on
proposals.reversible: partly — the pages can be un-linked, but a declared URL cannot be un-submitted
proposals.sequence: 1 — it determines what DB-02 and DB-03 are rewriting

proposals.title: Publish a named byline with a true one-line scope statement
proposals.what_changes: Every reader-facing article carries an author and a sentence saying what that person actually did — for example, that they read the three listings and the manufacturer pages on a stated date. Never 'tested'.
proposals.why: Google asks whether content demonstrates first-hand expertise and whether there is background about the author (BR-16). The FTC is blunter: you cannot talk about experience with a product you have not tried (BR-18). A byline that states the real scope is both the honest answer and the strongest trust signal available without a testing programme.

options.label: Real name, true scope sentence, dated
options.tradeoff: Best for trust; requires the owner to be named publicly.

options.label: Desk name (Counter Notes) with a true scope sentence
options.tradeoff: No personal exposure; weaker on the expertise signal Google describes.

options.label: No byline until a testing programme exists
options.tradeoff: Safest, and leaves the trust signal on the table indefinitely.

proposals.effort: estimate: an hour plus the decision
proposals.risk: estimate: low in itself; the decision of whether to be named is the owner's
proposals.recommended_note: B if the owner prefers not to be named publicly.

proposals.title: Set body text at 18–19px on a 62–70 character measure
proposals.what_changes: Body size up from the browser default, measure down from the current wide grid, serif display headlines, humanist sans for body. Cards and trust strips move below the fold.
proposals.why: Small text on a long measure is the look of a rendered table, and it is the second-largest contributor to the generated feel after the vocabulary. This is a craft judgement, not a rule; no official source states a font size.

options.label: Apply to the reader-facing surface first
options.tradeoff: The pages a visitor sees change; the evidence tables keep their density.

options.label: Apply across every namespace
options.tradeoff: Consistent, but the dense evidence tables were designed to be dense.

proposals.title: Set a re-verification cadence, or take the dates off the pages
proposals.what_changes: Either commit to re-fetching the load-bearing official pages on a stated interval and reprinting the date, or stop printing verification dates altogether.
proposals.why: Every page on the site prints a verification date that is already between one and three days old, and the oldest date any page prints is 2026-11-13. Google warns against changing dates to make content seem fresh when it has not substantively changed. A date that no one maintains is worse than no date: it is a claim that decays silently.

options.label: Quarterly re-verification, date printed and enforced by a gate
options.tradeoff: Highest integrity, and a recurring cost.

options.label: Re-verify only when a page is edited
options.tradeoff: Cheap; the date stops meaning 'checked' and starts meaning 'written'.

options.label: Remove printed dates
options.tradeoff: Honest and free, and loses a genuine differentiator.

proposals.effort: estimate: an hour to set the interval; a day to build the gate that enforces it
proposals.recommended_note: C if the site is going to be parked rather than pursued.

proposals.title: Derive the two stale counts on the readiness board and remove the duplicated suggestion row
proposals.what_changes: Replace RR-01's typed '116 published HTML pages' and RR-05's typed '72 pages link to amazon.com/dp/' with measured tokens, and resolve SG-11 / SG-12 into one row.
proposals.why: These are the only two typed counts left on a board whose entire purpose is to be checkable (FB-01, FB-02), and the duplicated row makes the suggestion board advertise twelve proposals where eleven exist (FB-03).

options.label: Derive both counts and delete the duplicate
options.tradeoff: Correct, and touches files owned by earlier sessions' scopes.

options.label: Log it as a change request and leave it
options.tradeoff: No conflict risk; the defects stay published.

proposals.risk: estimate: low, but it is outside this session's file scope and is logged as change request CR-1 instead of being done
proposals.recommended_note: It sits outside this session's file scope, so it is logged as change request CR-1 rather than done.

proposals.title: Instrument the site before writing another article
proposals.what_changes: Once a tag exists, add click-level measurement of the outbound product links and a dated record of what was clicked. Until then, write nothing new.
proposals.why: Every other proposal on this board is a judgement about what readers want, and today there is not one measured reader. Amazon's page states plainly that it makes no representation about the traffic or commission income any associate can expect (BR-06); the only way to replace that with knowledge is to measure this site.

options.label: Instrument first, then write
options.tradeoff: Slower to publish; every later editorial decision has evidence behind it.

options.label: Write the ten posts Amazon's content bar asks for, then instrument
options.tradeoff: Clears the application bar sooner; the second ten articles get written blind too.

proposals.effort: estimate: a day of work, but it cannot start until the tag exists
proposals.sequence: blocked — cannot start until the tag exists (BQ-14) and the account is approved (BQ-19)
proposals.recommended_note: A otherwise: instrument first, then write.

proposals.title: Re-fetch the manufacturer pages, or date the carry
proposals.what_changes: Re-read the Chefman and Emeril Lagasse product pages and re-quote the specification rows, or mark the published specs with the date they were last read and the fact that they were carried.
proposals.why: This session re-fetched the three Amazon destination listings and every program and ranking rule it quotes, but not the manufacturer pages (FB-08, BR-22). The specifications on the site are therefore one or two days older than the listings they sit beside.

options.label: Re-fetch and re-quote
options.tradeoff: Everything on the site is read on one date.

options.label: Date the carry and move on
options.tradeoff: Honest and free; the specs stay as old as they are.

proposals.recommended_note: Fold it into whatever cadence DB-09 sets.
